name: Syndactyly Type 3
aliases: Complete Syndactyly of Fourth and Fifth Fingers

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Syndactyly Type 3

criteria.description: Complete soft tissue and bony fusion between the fourth and fifth digits
No associated limb malformations outside the fourth and fifth digits
Radiographic evidence of bony fusion between phalanges of affected digits
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete syndactyly between fourth and fifth digits confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

imaging: X-ray demonstrating bony fusion between phalanges of fourth and fifth digits
Ultrasound may show soft tissue syndactyly
other: Physical examination revealing complete syndactyly of fourth and fifth fingers

distinguishingFeatures: Syndactyly involving third and fourth digits rather than fourth and fifth
Presence of localized absence of skin rather than fusion of digits

redFlags: Presence of syndactyly involving multiple digits beyond fourth and fifth
Signs of neurovascular compromise in affected digits
Associated craniofacial or systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Syndactyly
Fitzpatrick's Dermatology in General Medicine, 9th Edition
